title: Powerhouse ships two demonstration platforms: Vetra for builders and Achra for decentralized operations
content:
The host applications — Connect, Switchboard, Fusion, Renown — are infrastructure. On top of them Powerhouse launched two named platforms whose stated purpose is to demonstrate what the tech stack can build:

- **Vetra Builder Platform** (vetra.io) — "sovereign infrastructure for scalable network organizations — local first, built to scale." This is the builder-facing platform: where document models, editors, processors, and packages are specified, generated, and published.
- **Achra Decentralized Operations Platform** (achra.com) — "where open organizations can procure and purchase services." This is the operations-facing platform: the surface on which organizations scope work, choose providers, and transact.

## Why the pairing matters

The two platforms are the concrete instantiation of a distinction that runs through Powerhouse's strategy documents: a builder platform that governs *creation* of reusable modules, and an operations platform that runs *daily coordination*. The abstract pair is discussed frequently; the names attached to them are easy to miss. Vetra is the builder platform. Achra is the decentralized operations platform. If you have read about "the Builder Platform" and "the Decentralized Operations Platform" as roles, these are the products filling them.

## How to read "demonstration"

Neither is positioned as the product being sold. They exist to show that the stack — Reactor, Connect, Switchboard, Fusion, Renown — composes into real platforms, and to serve as the reference implementation others fork or extend for their own network organizations. Vetra in particular doubles as the builder toolchain Powerhouse itself develops with, which is why its name also attaches to concrete developer surfaces (Vetra Studio, the Vetra registry, Vetra Cloud) rather than only to a platform brand.

Both sit on the same substrate: Vetra builds and publishes the modules; Achra is one kind of organization-facing platform assembled from them.
